item.text: {"text":"Recent evidence supports separating recency dependence, contextualization, and component reliance. [Robust Training of Sequential Recommender Systems with Missing Input Data (2024)](https://iris.uniroma1.it/bitstream/11573/1740238/1/Siciliano_Robust-Training_2024.pdf) finds SASRec rankings much more sensitive to deleting the latest interaction than earlier interactions; ordinary dropout does not eliminate this sensitivity. [Residual Dominance (RecSys 2026)](https://programs.sigchi.org/recsys/2026/program/content/264578) reports localized last-item reliance in SASRec-style models. [Spotify’s 2026 benchmark study](https://research.atspotify.com/2026/10/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling) motivates comparisons with recency-weighted transition models and separate popularity adjustments. These findings support testing recent versus older history and residual pathways separately; sensitivity alone does not establish a fault.\n\n[Metamorphic testing for recommender systems (2024)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0950584924000156) demonstrates six relations across three recommender libraries, supporting diagnosis through controlled input/output relationships without exact-output oracles. Proposed application: validate probes against deliberately injected history-insensitive, popularity-only, shuffled-position, and disabled-component controls; report which faults each probe detects. Use fixed candidates, HR@10 changes, rank displacement, and top-k overlap; verify invariance under strictly increasing score transformations with consistent tie handling. Compare matched-count recent/older deletions, reporting sequence-length, padding, position, and item-frequency shifts. Treat inference ablations as acute interventions rather than evidence about retrained architectures. Preserve `DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` and `run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)` returning metrics and definitions; restore parameters, buffers, hooks, training modes, and RNG state in `finally`. These implementation recommendations are a synthesis, not a published validated suite."}
